# groundlens

> A proofreader for RAG answers. Given a model's answer and the passages it was
> supposed to be written from, groundlens returns the words those passages do not
> support, and names the closest span it found in each source. It returns no
> verdict: no pass, no fail, no probability, and no default threshold.

groundlens is a Python library, a CLI, and an MCP server. Apache-2.0. The core
package has zero runtime dependencies; a sentence-transformers encoder is an
optional extra needed only to read text.

## What it produces

For every word of the answer it emits an anchor: the word, its character span,
its support in 0.0-1.0, and the source span that supplied that support. The
answer-level figure, called the floor, is the mean of the k weakest anchors,
with k=1 by default. The mean over all anchors is deliberately not reported --
one wrong digit among sixty correct words disappears into an average.

A typical two-line output:

```
4.75%   support 0.00    nearest in policy.pdf#p3: '3.90%'
45      support 0.00    nearest in policy.pdf#p3: '30'
```

The second half of each line is the point. Other tools mark suspicious spans;
this one also names what the span should have matched, which is what lets a
human resolve it in seconds instead of re-reading the sources.

## Two channels

Words are decided by geometry: the highest cosine a word reaches against any
word in the sources, from a frozen encoder pinned by revision. Reproducible to
1e-6 across platforms with stable ordering, and not bit-identical between x86
and Apple Silicon.

Numbers are decided by arithmetic: parsed to a Decimal after format
normalisation, then compared for value equality. Support for a numeral is
exactly 1.0 or exactly 0.0, never in between, and it reproduces byte for byte on
any machine. Locale is an explicit argument, never read from the environment;
left as "und", an ambiguous numeral keeps every valid reading rather than
guessing one.

The numeral channel exists because the geometric one cannot do that job.
Changing 10,000 to 1,000 in a sentence barely moves its meaning, and for a
reviewer at a bank that digit is the whole document.

## Why there is no threshold

Across 45 detector-benchmark combinations measured at the operating point
production runs at -- the false-positive rate required to catch 95% of
hallucinations -- the best result was 0.65. A shipped threshold would be a
control that escalates most correct answers. If you need a cut, `calibrate()`
derives one from your own labelled data (minimum 200 examples) and hands back
the false-positive rate and its 95% confidence interval alongside it, so the
cost is visible before deployment.

## API

```python
from groundlens import proofread, SentenceTransformerEncoder

marks = proofread(
    answer,                                   # str, the model output
    [("policy.pdf#p3", passage)],             # (source_id, text) pairs
    encoder=SentenceTransformerEncoder(),     # required; no default encoder
    k=1,                                      # anchors averaged into the floor
    locale="und",                             # "en", "es", "de", ... or "und"
)

marks.floor        # float
marks.weakest      # the k anchors that produced it, weakest first
marks.anchors      # every word, in answer order
marks.report()     # the receipt lines above, as text
marks.sha256       # digest of the structural result, for reproducibility
```

`Anchor` carries `text`, `span`, `kind` ("numeral" or "lexical"), `support`,
`value`, `evidence_id`, `evidence_text`, `evidence_span`, `notes`. `Proofread`
has no `decision` field, by design.

Any object satisfying the `Encoder` protocol works -- `id`, `max_tokens`,
`token_spans()`, `encode_window()` -- so the library is testable without
downloading a model. Answers longer than one encoder window are handled by
sliding windows aligned on character spans, so no word past the token cap is
silently dropped.

## Interfaces

```bash
pip install "groundlens[encoder]"
groundlens read --answer answer.txt --context policy.pdf#p3=policy.txt
```

The MCP server exposes exactly one tool, `find_unsupported_words`, so an
assistant can proofread an answer inside a conversation.

## What it is used for

A reviewer at a bank, an insurer, a law firm or a benefits agency has an answer
drafted by a retrieval system, three retrieved passages, and a signature to
give. Reading all four documents takes five minutes and mostly does not happen.
Marks in a margin take thirty seconds. groundlens is built to make that person
fast, not to replace them.
